free.title: West Indian American Day Carnival
free.caption:
FREE · CROWN HEIGHTS

One million people, one parkway - the West Indian American Day Carnival turns 59 this Labor Day, and watching is completely free.

Brooklyn's Eastern Parkway becomes a river of feathers, flags and steel pan from 11AM. Mas bands roll from Utica Ave to Grand Army Plaza all afternoon, with soca trucks and jerk smoke the whole way. It is the largest Caribbean carnival in the country and one of the last great free spectacles in New York.

Local move: ride the 3 to Kingston Ave and skip the Utica crush entirely.

Tag the friend who already owns a flag.

art.title: Banksy Museum
art.caption:
ART · CHINATOWN

The world's largest Banksy collection is not in London - it sits above a corner of Canal Street in Chinatown.

The Banksy Museum rebuilds his most famous street pieces at life size, from Girl with Balloon to the Bristol walls that started it all. No tiny frames, no velvet ropes - you stand in front of the murals the way the street saw them, all in about an hour.

Go after 6PM: the rush thins out and last entry is 7:15. It is also one of the rare big NYC art stops without timed tickets, so you can wander in on a whim.

Share this with someone who still thinks street art belongs outside.
